newsitem.title: ITALY: Bologna soccer club choose Nomura for flotation.
newsitem.headline: Bologna soccer club choose Nomura for flotation.

text.p: Italian soccer club Bologna has appointed Nomura investment bank to manage its proposed stock market flotation, Nomura said on Tuesday.
The bank said in a statement that Nomura International and its brokerage Nomura Italia SIM would coordinate a capital increase and an initial public offering of shares.
It said the flotation was expected during the next Italian soccer season, which runs from the end of August 1997 to May 1998.
Bologna, who finished seventh in last season's Italian championship, had said previously they planned to list.
Rome-based club Lazio said on Monday they would go to market before the end of the year.

A flotation in Italy is problematic because most clubs do not meet the disclosure rules applicable on the Milan bourse or requirements for three straight years of profit prior to a listing, share analysts say.
However, the Italian government last year opened the way for clubs to list on the stock exchange by passing a decree law allowing them to become profit-making corporations.
